verdict.summary: You create the OAuth app with the HubSpot CLI and connect your own account in under an hour, with no review. Other accounts can install it straight away if they click through an unverified-app warning. HubSpot only reviews Marketplace listings, and you can't apply for one until at least 3 unaffiliated production accounts are actively using the app.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 hours for a working app. A Marketplace listing adds 1-3 days of work: setup guide, legal pages, removing unused scopes.
verdict.approval_wait: None to install. A Marketplace listing gets a first review within 10 business days, and the full feedback cycle can run up to about 60 days.

gates.name: Your own account
gates.unlocks: You upload the app as a project and connect your own HubSpot account (or a developer test account) through your own client ID and the Composio callback.
limits: New apps must be built on the new developer platform (Projects), because legacy public apps can no longer be created after June 23, 2026
Access tokens expire after 30 minutes, so your app has to refresh them
The person installing must be a Super Admin or have HubSpot Marketplace Access permission

gates.name: Test installs / standard installs (unverified)
gates.unlocks: Developer test accounts (Distribution > Test installs) and other standard HubSpot accounts (Distribution > Standard install) can install the app.
limits: An unverified app shows a warning when someone installs it. The installer must tick a checkbox, or type 'I accept the risk', before they can connect
If you choose specific-accounts distribution, only allowlisted accounts can install
Installer must be a Super Admin or have Marketplace Access permission

gates.name: HubSpot Marketplace listing (optional Certification)
gates.unlocks: A public listing on the HubSpot Marketplace, plus an optional Certified badge. Accounts can install without a listing, but they see the unverified-app warning.
limits: You need at least 3 active, unique installs in unaffiliated production accounts within the last 30 days
You can have only one listing submission in review at a time
From Nov 2, 2026 the app must be on platform version v2025.2 or v2026.03 and use the OAuth v3 endpoints
Certification needs 60 or more active installs, a security questionnaire, a verified domain and a demo video. It must be renewed every 2 years
HubSpot charges no fee to list or certify an app
gates.time_to_reach: Weeks. You first need 3 active unaffiliated installs, then the first review takes up to 10 business days, and the feedback cycle up to about 60 days.

steps.title: Get a HubSpot developer account
steps.detail: Sign in to (or create) the HubSpot developer account that will own the app. Also create a developer test account so you can install the app without touching production data.
gotchas: The findings don't say whether a free developer account is enough or whether you need a paid plan or partner enrollment. See open questions.

steps.title: Create the app project with the HubSpot CLI
steps.detail: Install the HubSpot CLI and run 'hs project create'. When asked about distribution, choose HubSpot Marketplace if you want any account to be able to install, or restrict installs to specific accounts. Choose OAuth as the auth type.
gotchas: Legacy public apps can no longer be created (since June 23, 2026)
A static token only works for a single account. Multi-account apps and listed apps must use OAuth

steps.title: Declare the redirect URL and scopes in app-hsmeta.json
steps.detail: In the 'auth' block of app-hsmeta.json, add the Composio callback to 'redirectUrls'. Put the scopes your agent actually uses into 'requiredScopes', and the nice-to-have ones into 'optionalScopes'.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

values.label: requiredScopes
values.value: Only the scopes your tools use, e.g. crm.objects.contacts.read, crm.objects.contacts.write

gotchas: Redirect URLs must use https. Plain http is only allowed for localhost, and IP addresses are rejected
Composio's default scope list is very broad. Requiring scopes the installing account's tier doesn't support can break installs, so move those to optionalScopes

steps.title: Upload the project
steps.detail: Run 'hs project upload' to deploy the app. Re-run it whenever you change app-hsmeta.json.

steps.title: Copy the client credentials
steps.detail: Open the project details page, go to the app's Auth tab and, under Client credentials, copy the Client ID and Client secret.

steps.title: Create a Composio auth config with your credentials
steps.detail: In Composio, create a HubSpot OAuth2 auth config that uses your own credentials. Paste in the Client ID and secret, and enter the same scopes you declared in app-hsmeta.json. Check that the callback URL shown matches the redirectUrls entry exactly.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Composio's managed config points to the /oauth/v1/token endpoint. HubSpot requires the OAuth v3 endpoints for new listings, so confirm which token endpoint your config uses before you submit a listing

steps.title: Connect your own or test account
steps.detail: Start a connection from Composio, or add a test install under Projects > your app > Distribution > Test installs, and approve the scopes. To pin the authorization to one account, put the account ID between /oauth/ and /authorize in the authorize URL.
gotchas: The installer must be a Super Admin or have HubSpot Marketplace Access permission
Access tokens get the app's scopes, not the installing user's own permissions

steps.title: Verify token exchange and refresh
steps.detail: Run a test authorization and confirm the code is exchanged at /oauth/v3/token. Then confirm the access token, which lasts 30 minutes, is refreshed with the refresh token before it expires.
gotchas: How long refresh tokens last isn't documented officially. Only a community post says they never expire

steps.title: Let other accounts install
steps.detail: Send other accounts a Composio connect link, or install through Distribution > Standard install. The installer will see an unverified-app warning and must tick the checkbox (or type 'I accept the risk') before clicking Connect.

steps.title: Prepare Marketplace listing materials
steps.detail: Draft a public setup guide (no paywall or sign-in) that covers install, connecting the account with screenshots of the scope approval screen, configuration, use, disconnecting and uninstalling. Also prepare live Terms of Service and Privacy Policy URLs, support resources, an Install button URL, Shared data entries that match your scopes, and pricing that matches your website. Remove any scope the app doesn't use.
gotchas: Classic CRM cards are not allowed

steps.title: Get 3 active unaffiliated installs
steps.detail: Before you submit, at least 3 unique production accounts that aren't affiliated with your organization must have used the app successfully within the past 30 days.

steps.title: Submit the listing
steps.detail: Check that the app is on platform version v2025.2 or v2026.03, uses the OAuth v3 endpoints, and authorizes requests with the app ID and client ID tied to the listing. Then submit the listing for review.
gotchas: From Nov 2, 2026, listings built on legacy apps or Projects 2023.2/2025.1 will be rejected
A second submission sent while one is in review is rejected automatically
Composio's managed client can't be used for the listing

steps.title: Wait for the Ecosystem Quality review
steps.detail: HubSpot reviews listings manually and finishes the first review within 10 business days. Answering feedback can take up to about 60 days.

steps.title: Optional: apply for Certification
steps.detail: Once you have 60 or more active unaffiliated installs, complete the security questionnaire and verify your domain. You also need to keep the API success rate above 95% and send a demo video of disconnecting and uninstalling. Certification lasts 2 years.

requirements.detail: Required for any app installed by more than one account or listed on the Marketplace.
Only localhost may use http. IP addresses are not accepted.
The person installing must be a Super Admin or have HubSpot Marketplace Access permission.
Unique production accounts, not affiliated with you, with successful app activity in the past 30 days.
Covers install, connecting (with scope screenshots), configuration, use, disconnecting and uninstalling. No paywall or sign-in.

requirements.item: Live Terms of Service and Privacy Policy, support resources, Install button URL
requirements.detail: Shared data must match the requested scopes, and listed pricing must match your website.

requirements.item: Supported platform version and OAuth v3
requirements.detail: v2025.2 or v2026.03 from Nov 2, 2026. New listings must use the OAuth v3 endpoints.
100 inbound requests every 10 seconds per connected account.
60+ active installs, security questionnaire, verified domain, >95% API success rate, uninstall demo video.

scopes.effect: HubSpot adds this to every app automatically.

scopes.scope: crm.objects.contacts.read / crm.objects.contacts.write (and other standard CRM scopes)
scopes.effect: Declare them in requiredScopes or optionalScopes. Reviewers expect every requested scope to be used and will ask you to remove extras.
The installer can accept or decline each one. Use this for scopes that depend on the account's tier, so installs don't fail when one isn't available.
Enterprise accounts only, and not allowed for Marketplace-listed apps.

blockers.symptom: You can't create a legacy public app
blockers.cause: Legacy public app creation closed on June 23, 2026.
blockers.fix: Build on the new developer platform with 'hs project create'.

blockers.symptom: Listing rejected for an unsupported platform version
blockers.cause: From Nov 2, 2026, listings built on legacy apps or Projects 2023.2/2025.1 are rejected.
blockers.fix: Build on, or migrate to, v2025.2 or v2026.03. Apps going through certification get about 60 days to migrate.

blockers.symptom: Listing rejected for the OAuth endpoint version
blockers.cause: New listings must use the OAuth v3 endpoints. Composio's managed config points to /oauth/v1/token.
blockers.fix: Make sure the token exchange uses /oauth/v3/token before you submit.

blockers.cause: Only one app can be in listing review at a time.
blockers.fix: Wait until the current review finishes before you submit another app.

blockers.cause: The app requests scopes it doesn't use, or sensitive-data scopes.
blockers.fix: Remove unused and sensitive scopes, and make Shared data match the scopes you keep.

blockers.symptom: Listing rejected because the client ID doesn't match
blockers.cause: The listing must authorize requests with its own app ID and client ID. Composio's managed app has a different client ID.
blockers.fix: Use your own app's credentials in Composio.

composio.note: Composio's managed HubSpot app is the fastest way to prototype. Its default scope list is broad, though, and the research notes that some defaults, such as the custom-object scopes, may be Enterprise-only. Register your own app when you need your own branding on the consent screen, a trimmed scope list, or a Marketplace listing. A listing has to use its own app ID and client ID, so Composio's managed client won't qualify. In your auth config, paste your Client ID and secret, and put Composio's callback URL into redirectUrls in app-hsmeta.json.

evidence.claim: Legacy public app creation was closed on June 23, 2026.
evidence.quote: As of June 23, 2026, legacy public apps can no longer be created.

evidence.claim: New-platform apps are created with 'hs project create', choosing the distribution and the auth type.
evidence.quote: select whether you plan to distribute your app on the HubSpot Marketplace or if want to restrict installation to specific HubSpot accounts.

evidence.claim: The Client ID and secret are on the app's Auth tab, under Client credentials.
evidence.quote: Under *Client credentials*, copy the *Client ID* and *Client secret* from your new app

evidence.claim: Redirect URLs and scopes are declared in the auth block of app-hsmeta.json and deployed with hs project upload.
evidence.quote: edit the corresponding scopes within the `auth` property of your app's `app-hsmeta.json` file locally, then run the `hs project upload` command

evidence.claim: Redirect URIs must use https in production; http is allowed only for localhost.
evidence.quote: For security reasons, this URL must use `https` in production. (When testing using `localhost`, `http` can be used.)

evidence.claim: The authorize URL can be scoped to one account by adding the account ID.
evidence.quote: You can set the authorization URL to be for a specific HubSpot account by adding the account ID between `/oauth/` and `/authorize`

evidence.claim: The authorization code is exchanged at /oauth/v3/token.
evidence.quote: You'll then make an API request to `/oauth/v3/token` with a request body that includes the `code`, the `redirect_uri`, your app's `client_id` and `client_secret`

evidence.claim: Installers must be a Super Admin or have Marketplace Access permission.
evidence.quote: Users installing apps in their HubSpot account must either be a Super Admin or have HubSpot Marketplace Access permissions.

evidence.claim: Multi-account or listed apps must use OAuth.
evidence.quote: Any app designed for installation by multiple HubSpot accounts or listing on the HubSpot Marketplace must use OAuth.

evidence.claim: Unverified apps show a warning, and the installer must type an acceptance phrase.
evidence.quote: type **I accept the risk**, and click **Connect** to authorize the app.

evidence.claim: Test installs are added under Distribution > Test installs.
evidence.quote: On the *Distribution* tab, next to *Test installs*, click **Add test install(s)**.

evidence.claim: A standard install requires ticking a checkbox to authorize an unverified app.
evidence.quote: Select the **checkbox** to authorize installing an unverified app, then click **Connect app**.

evidence.claim: A listing requires OAuth and at least 3 active unaffiliated installs in the last 30 days.
evidence.quote: Active installs are the number of unique HubSpot production accounts, unaffiliated with your organization, showing successful app activity within the past 30 days.

evidence.claim: Listings are reviewed manually and rejected if they don't meet the criteria.
evidence.quote: App listing submissions are manually reviewed by the HubSpot Ecosystem Quality team and will be rejected if they do not meet the criteria outlined below.

evidence.claim: A listing requires a public setup guide URL.
evidence.quote: In order for an app to be listed or certified on the HubSpot Marketplace, the listing must include a publicly available setup guide URL.

evidence.claim: A listing needs live ToS and Privacy Policy URLs, support resources, an Install URL, matching Shared data and matching pricing.
evidence.quote: URLs for your app's Terms of Service and Privacy Policy must be live and up-to-date.

evidence.claim: Listed apps must not use sensitive-data scopes.
evidence.quote: Your app must not access, request, or use

evidence.claim: Listed apps cannot use classic CRM cards.
evidence.quote: your app cannot use classic CRM cards, as they are no longer supported as of June 16, 2025.

evidence.claim: Only one app can be in listing review at a time.
evidence.quote: you can only submit one app at a time for approval.

evidence.claim: The first review takes up to 10 business days; the full process takes up to 60 days from feedback.
evidence.quote: the HubSpot Ecosystem Quality team will complete an initial review within 10 business days.

evidence.claim: HubSpot charges no fee to list or certify.
evidence.quote: No, we do not charge you a fee to list or certify your apps in the HubSpot Marketplace, nor a fee for installs generated through the HubSpot Marketplace.

evidence.claim: Certification requires a security questionnaire and a verified domain.
evidence.quote: You must also complete a security questionnaire addressing questions of encryption, access controls, and token lifecycle management

evidence.claim: Certification requires 60+ active unique installs.
evidence.quote: Your app must have at least 60 [active](#activity), unique installs to qualify for and retain certification.

evidence.claim: Certification requires an API success rate above 95%.
evidence.quote: Maintain an average success rate above **95%** across all [activities](#activity).

evidence.claim: Apps should respect 100 requests per 10 seconds per account.
evidence.quote: Respecting rate limits (i.e. 100 inbound requests every 10 seconds per connected HubSpot account).

evidence.claim: Certification requires a disconnect/uninstall demo video.
evidence.quote: when removing the app from a customer's HubSpot account.

evidence.claim: Certification is valid for two years and must be renewed.
evidence.quote: App certifications are valid on a rolling basis for two years, and must be renewed.

evidence.claim: From Nov 2, 2026, listings must be on v2025.2 or v2026.03.
evidence.quote: Starting **November 2, 2026**: Apps must be on a supported developer platform version (v2025.2 or v2026.03).

evidence.claim: Apps in certification get about 60 days to migrate.
evidence.quote: Apps undergoing certification or recertification will have ~60 days to migrate to a supported version

evidence.claim: New listings and certifications must use the OAuth v3 endpoints.
evidence.quote: all new app listings, certification submissions, and apps undergoing recertification, must use the new OAuth v3 endpoints.

evidence.claim: Optional scopes are sent in optional_scope, and the user can decline them.
evidence.quote: Optional scopes: scopes that are not required to successfully install your app. These scopes are included in the `optional_scope` query parameter

evidence.claim: Extraneous scopes must be removed.
evidence.quote: Extraneous scopes must be removed.

evidence.claim: Sensitive-data scopes are Enterprise-only.
evidence.quote: Available to *Enterprise* accounts only.

evidence.claim: The oauth scope is added to all apps by default.
evidence.quote: This scope is added by default to all apps.

evidence.claim: Access tokens expire after 30 minutes.
evidence.quote: Access tokens are short-lived (30 minutes), and you can check the expires_in parameter

evidence.claim: A community post says refresh tokens never expire (unofficial).
evidence.quote: HubSpot OAuth Refresh Tokens never expire.

evidence.claim: Access tokens reflect the app's scopes, not the user's permissions.
evidence.quote: Access tokens reflect the scopes requested from the app and do not reflect the permissions or limitations of what a user can do in their HubSpot account.

evidence.claim: A listing must authorize requests with its own app ID and client ID.
evidence.quote: your app must authorize API requests with the public HubSpot app ID (and OAuth client ID) associated with your app listing.

evidence.claim: The developer docs load without a login wall.
A self-owned app must register its exact redirect URI, so Composio's managed app can't be reused for a self-owned listing.
Composio's managed HubSpot config uses the token URL https://api.hubapi.com/oauth/v1/token, which differs from the v3 endpoints HubSpot requires for new listings.

open_questions: Is a free HubSpot developer account enough to create an app, or do you need a paid plan or Technology Partner enrollment?
Is there a cap on how many accounts can install an unlisted Marketplace-distribution app on the new platform? The findings don't say.
What are the verified-domain steps for new-platform apps? The DNS TXT steps found apply only to legacy apps.
Do refresh tokens expire? Only a community post says they don't.
Does the Composio auth config let you set the token URL to /oauth/v3/token for a self-owned app?
Which Composio default scopes need specific HubSpot tiers? They weren't checked one by one.
Must the redirect_uri exactly match a registered redirectUrls entry on the new platform? This is confirmed for legacy apps only.
How long do reviews take in practice beyond HubSpot's official 10 business days / 60 days? This is unknown.
